answer.note: The handoff_refs files are identical boilerplate and name no file, so I chose from the code. D (dogwhistle/honest.py) is the match. Its `_verify_history` (lines 175-195) rejects `prereg_commit == ledger_commit`. It also requires `git diff --name-only` between the two commits to equal only the public digest file. It uses the two arms in `ARMS`. Spend about 40 of the 60 minutes on D. C (dogwhistle/visibility.py) is the second pick, with about 12 minutes. It is the closest two-arm sibling, and its history check at line 192 has the ancestor and anchor checks but no equal-commit or changed-files check, so it needs a regression comparison against D. Spend about 8 minutes skimming A (study.py) and B (heldout.py). Their `verify_history` functions use three commits (prereg, seal, ledger). They check ancestry and anchors, but they don't reject equal commits or check which files changed. I only read the history functions, and I did not run any tests.

input.note: The handoff_refs files are identical boilerplate and name no file, so I chose from the code. D (dogwhistle/honest.py) is the match. Its `_verify_history` (lines 175-195) rejects `prereg_commit == ledger_commit`. It also requires `git diff --name-only` between the two commits to equal only the public digest file. It uses the two arms in `ARMS`. Spend about 40 of the 60 minutes on D. C (dogwhistle/visibility.py) is the second pick, with about 12 minutes. It is the closest two-arm sibling, and its history check at line 192 has the ancestor and anchor checks but no equal-commit or changed-files check, so it needs a regression comparison against D. Spend about 8 minutes skimming A (study.py) and B (heldout.py). Their `verify_history` functions use three commits (prereg, seal, ledger). They check ancestry and anchors, but they don't reject equal commits or check which files changed. I only read the history functions, and I did not run any tests.
